content_of_post_to_comment:
For the longest time, I thought productive people were just more motivated than everyone else. So I'd wait until I "felt like it." Some days I’d get a lot of stuff done, but with 3 TBIs and PTSD from combat, there were many days that I didn’t feel like getting out of bed, much less doing anything. I would be doomscrolling, procrastinating, waiting for things to be perfect before I would start and thinking/hoping/fooling myself that tomorrow would be different.

The biggest shift for me wasn't finding more motivation. It was realizing motivation is one of the least reliable things to build your life around. Thank you, Scott Adams, for teaching me Systems Over Goals. With this new mindset, I now try to make progress whether I feel motivated or not.

A few things that made the biggest difference:

I lowered the bar to start. Instead of "finish the project," it's "work for five minutes." Starting is usually the hardest part. If I don’t feel like working out, I do as Scott Adams recommended and drive to the gym and once I am there, it is a lot harder to skip the workout2. I stopped judging my feelings. I don't need to want to do something to begin doing it.

I focus on consistency over intensity. One hour every day beats a random 10-hour burst once a month.

I measure success by showing up, not by having the perfect session. Some days are amazing. Some days I just maintain the habit. Both count.

One thing I've noticed is that motivation often shows up after I've started, not before. Action creates momentum far more often than waiting for inspiration. See the example in 1 as it applies here too.

I'm still not perfectly disciplined. I still procrastinate sometimes. The TBIs and PTSD are always going to be challenges. The difference is I don't see a lack of motivation as a reason to stop anymore. I see motivation as a bonus and not a requirement.

I used this system last year to create an app from scratch, as well as a website and hundreds of hours in content in the space of 6 months. I had never programmed before, the work was intensely frustrating, and most days it would have been easier to ”not feel like it” and procrastinate. But my productivity was not contingent on my being motivated. I got it done to prove to myself that there was a way to get beyond the limitations I had been living with.

Question for everyone: What's one habit or system you've built that works even on days when you have zero motivation? My system worked for me, but I can always incorporate new ideas.
